title: Prospective bracketing of the target-label equivalent of pretraining

amendment.reason: The estimand was defined per architecture and target family, but the original activation gate required a persistent gain on both families. That would leave a real family-conditional gain unmeasured.
amendment.correction: Activate and bracket each architecture-family cell that independently passes the persistent material-gain rule. Reserve a broad label-saving claim for replicated savings on both families, and report any one-family result only as family-conditional.
amendment.information_boundary: This correction was made while the convergence extension was still running and without inspecting any continuation loss, validation metric, or test result.

materiality_amendment.reason: If scratch-80 matched pretrained-64, the original [64, 80] bracket could not decide the registered materiality claim that pretraining is worth more than 5% of the 64-case target budget. Its lower bound always included an immaterial saving.
materiality_amendment.correction: On the low branch only, add scratch-67 after scratch-80 matches. Because N_equiv is an integer, scratch-67 matching bounds the saving at 1-3 cases, while scratch-67 not matching proves N_equiv >= 68 and therefore a saving of at least 4 cases, which exceeds 5% of 64.
materiality_amendment.information_boundary: This correction and the pilot-only forecast below were frozen while the convergence extension was still running and without inspecting any continuation loss, validation metric, or test result.

information_boundary: Written while the pretrained-64 versus scratch-128 convergence extension was still running. No convergence-extension loss, validation metric, or test result was inspected.
scientific_question: If a same-budget pretraining gain persists but does not replace all 64 additional target vehicles, how many target-only training vehicles is that gain actually worth?

estimand.definition: For each architecture and target family, N_equiv is the smallest nested scratch-training sample count whose stabilized pressure error is no larger than the stabilized pretrained-64 pressure error at the same target-update budget.
estimand.scope: A validation-only, protocol-specific label equivalent. It is not a universal data-efficiency constant.

activation_gate.activate: For each architecture-family cell, activate if the architecture fails the half-label gate and that cell passes the prospectively amended persistent material same-budget-gain rule.
activation_gate.do_not_activate: If the half-label gate passes, confirm it across seeds and source checkpoints. Do not bracket a cell that passes the null-or-immaterial same-budget rule; it has no material positive label equivalent under this source protocol.
activation_gate.family_scope: If only one target family activates, run and interpret only that family. This can support a family-conditional saving after replication, not a broad source-reuse claim.

nested_sample_counts.construction: Use the first N cases from the exact deterministic ordering in shift_suv_adaptation_design.py: sort each family's source-training cases by SHA256('shift-suv-adaptation-pilot-v1\0' + family + '\0' + case_id). This is the ordering that generated the existing nested 64- and 128-case subsets. No case may be selected by geometry, label, or validation performance.

case_list_sha256.hash_definition: SHA256 of lexicographically sorted case IDs joined by newline, including a final newline.
case_list_sha256.verification: The same ordering exactly reproduced the existing train_64 and train_128 sets for both families, reproduced the previously frozen 80/96/112 hashes, and all six counts were strictly nested.

adaptive_rule: For each activated architecture-family cell, train and stabilize scratch-96 first.
For that cell, if scratch-96 pressure error is no larger than pretrained-64 error on both full-validation and cross-fit reductions, train scratch-80.
If scratch-80 also matches pretrained-64, train scratch-67 to decide the registered 5%-of-64 materiality threshold.
For that cell, if scratch-96 pressure error is larger than pretrained-64 error on either reduction, train scratch-112.
Each cell follows only its selected path: 96 to 112, or 96 to 80 and then to 67 only if 80 matches. Different cells may select different paths.

controls.target_updates: Use the same final target-update budget as the convergence extension. If an epoch boundary cannot hit it exactly, stop by optimizer step rather than changing the sample count.
controls.optimization: Use the same continuation-rate grid, model-selection protocol, plateau gate, and outward-learning-rate-flank rule as the convergence extension.
controls.validation: Use the same 99 validation cases and two fixed point samples. Full-validation selection is descriptive; the frozen five-fold case cross-fit may block but not create a conclusion.
controls.field_safety: Wall-shear-stress error must not worsen by more than 10% relative to the pretrained-64 reference.
controls.test_policy: All SHIFT-SUV test cases remain sealed.

monotonicity_gate.requirement: Across every evaluated nested scratch count, pressure error must be nonincreasing with sample count within a 2% tolerance in both full-validation and cross-fit reductions.
monotonicity_gate.failure_interpretation: A larger target set performing materially worse means optimization or seed noise dominates the learning curve; N_equiv is not identifiable from these runs and no interpolation is allowed.

pilot_only_forecast.status: A non-decision forecast from the completed epoch-70 parent pilot; all parent curves were still improving and the continuation result was not inspected.
pilot_only_forecast.method: For each architecture-family cell, fit the two-point local scratch-only law error(N) proportional to N^(-alpha) from N=64 and N=128, then solve N_equiv = 64 * G_64^(1/alpha) using the pilot same-budget gain G_64.
pilot_only_forecast.interpretation: The adaptive 80/96/112 counts straddle the pilot forecasts, but the MeshTransformer-estate forecast lies close enough to the materiality boundary that scratch-67 is required for a decisive low-branch claim.

prospective_brackets.scratch_67_matches: Activation establishes that scratch-64 does not match. If scratch-67 matches, integer N_equiv is in [65, 67], so pretraining is worth 1-3 target vehicles and is immaterial under the registered greater-than-5%-of-64 rule.
prospective_brackets.scratch_67_does_not_match_but_scratch_80: Integer N_equiv is in [68, 80], so pretraining is worth 4-16 target vehicles and clears the registered materiality threshold before seed replication.
prospective_brackets.scratch_80_does_not_match_but_scratch_96: Integer N_equiv is in [81, 96], so pretraining is worth 17-32 additional target vehicles.
prospective_brackets.scratch_96_does_not_match_but_scratch_11: Integer N_equiv is in [97, 112], so pretraining is worth 33-48 additional target vehicles.
prospective_brackets.scratch_112_does_not_match_but_scratch_1: Integer N_equiv is in [113, 128], so pretraining is worth 49-64 additional target vehicles.
prospective_brackets.scratch_128_does_not_match: N_equiv lies above 128 and is not bracketed by this study. This does not retroactively pass the original half-label gate, whose 5% materiality and uncertainty requirements remain controlling.

decision.broad_material_partial_saving: Advance a broad partial label-saving claim only if the identified integer bracket implies N_equiv >= 68 on both target families and survives independent target-training seeds.
decision.family_conditional_partial_saving: If the same threshold and replication rule passes on exactly one family, report a family-conditional saving only; do not average it with or generalize it over the other family.
decision.architecture_claim_limit: Different single-seed brackets between architectures motivate replication; they do not establish that one architecture transfers better.
